mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively affecting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO MoM < -2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2%, it indicates a monetary policy mismatch that can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the trigger condition is met and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests strong labor market conditions, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the trigger condition is met and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for economic growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 5% and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is decreasing, it suggests a favorable environment for business expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the trigger condition is met and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
